Sixpenny Money, X:3

Heard this version played by Seamus Ennis and Ken Rickets, it is played in a rather tight or staccato style.

Late in Seamus Ennis’ piping career he started to play in a tighter style. Whether it was intentional or not, I do not know.

↳ Posted by Sean Perry on August 1st, 2024.

Sixpenny Money, X:10

This is the basic version of the tune I learned many years ago from Peter Fitzgerald. I’m dusting this tune off now. Not seeing it here, I thought to add it. For variations on tenor banjo, some of the rolls become triplets or cran-like quadruplets, some become quarter note-eighth note couplets. Launching into this tune always gave the dancers a lift. Pair it with Tenpenny Bit.
